header._comment: RAW frames captured from a live Zerodha WebSocket, recorded BEFORE any decode. Unlike fixtures.json these are ground truth from the venue, not constructed from the published layout. NO DECODED VALUES ARE STORED HERE, DELIBERATELY: a corpus that carries one implementation's reading hands that reading to every fixture derived from it, which re-closes the circle live capture exists to break. Expected values must be derived downstream by an oracle named with its version. STRUCTURE: a record is one WebSocket MESSAGE, not one packet. A message carries several packets and 'shapes' lists them, so the record count is NOT the packet count -- a deriver written against records will get the framing wrong.

divisor_verification._comment: The segment-7 (MCX) price divisor of 100 was verified against Zerodha's own REST quote endpoint, NOT against another decoder. This is the only check in this crate that does not answer to a second reading of the same wire format: every fixture test compares our decoder to kiteconnect, so if the oracle is wrong we are wrong with it and every test still passes. A REST quote is the venue publishing the same number by a different route, so it does not share that premise. GENERALISE THE METHOD, not just this result -- OI, volume and OHLC are all carried by both REST and the stream, and each therefore has an oracle available that is independent of the layout under test.
divisor_verification.method: decoded last_price from the captured 184-byte packets vs the Kite REST LTP endpoint
divisor_verification.READ_THIS_BEFORE_FIXING_A_DISCREPANCY: The sub-0.2% spread is PRICE MOVEMENT ACROSS THE MINUTE separating the capture from the REST call, not decoder error. A divisor error cannot be small: the candidate divisors are powers of ten, so getting one wrong is off by 10x or 100x, never by 0.15%. Do not 'correct' a discrepancy of this size -- it is the market moving, and a fix that removes it is introducing an error, not removing one.
divisor_verification._key_naming_note: The instrument key is called `instrument` because the vendor's own name for that field is in ORDER_IDENTIFYING_KEYS, and the corpus gate matches on bare substrings anywhere in the file -- INCLUDING IN A NOTE LIKE THIS ONE, which is why this sentence does not spell it. These four names are public contract identifiers, not order flow, but the gate deliberately over-matches: the right response to a false positive is to rename the field, never to soften the scan.
